newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Murdoch's son Lachlan takes over News in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch's son Lachlan takes over News in Australia.

text.p: Global media baron Rupert Murdoch said Tuesday his 25-year-old son, Lachlan, would take control of his company's sometimes troublesome Australian operations.

In a statement from Los Angeles, the News Corp. Ltd. founder and chief executive said Lachlan Murdoch would assume responsibility for the Australian offshoot, News Ltd., with the retirement of veteran aide Ken Cowley at the end of June.
The move puts Lachlan Murdoch in charge of a company which dominates Australia's newspaper markets -- and also puts a spotlight on 66-year-old Rupert Murdoch's own succession.

Lachlan Murdoch became managing director of the Australian unit in September 1996 and the following month leapfrogged his elder sister, Elisabeth, in the succession stakes when he was appointed to the board of the parent company, News Corp.
"As managing director of News Ltd., Mr. Lachlan Murdoch will assume overall responsibility for our Australian operations," Rupert Murdoch said.
Analysts said Lachlan Murdoch, who began working for News Ltd. three years ago after receiving a degree at Princeton University, will be firmly guided by his father, who is now a U.S. citizen.
The Australian operations dominate the capital city newspaper market and include magazines, a costly pay-television operation, and the Super League rugby league tournament which began this year.

News Corp. is also a partner with Air New Zealand in the money-losing Ansett Airlines. Cowley will remain a News Corp. board member and chairman of the Ansett company, as well as director of some other publicly traded firms controlled by News Corp.

Media analysts have speculated in the last year or so that either Lachlan, Murdoch's elder son, or Elisabeth, 28, would eventually take control of the international media firm once their father tires of the job.
"You would have to say Lachlan is the favoured one at this time," said an Australian analyst who asked not to be named.
"He is the only one on the board (of News Corp)."
Elisabeth is an executive with the News Corp. affiliate British Sky Broadcasting (BSB) in London.
Analysts were little concerned by Lachlan Murdoch's youth, noting he would be surrounded by experienced executives and would make few big decisions without reference to his father.
One said that at this stage of his career Lachlan Murdoch was older than his father was when he took control of his first newspaper, the Adelaide News, in Australia.
"How old was his dad when he took over -- 21? That is the question that everyone is going to be asking," the analyst said.
